source_links_enforced_means: The flag asserts that every MEASURED cell records all five mandated source layers with a date on each check; that a layer recorded as found carries what it yielded and a link resolving to that row's own trial identifier; and that a layer recorded as not available carries a reason and a date. title: Sotagliflozin against placebo across its pivotal cardiovascular outcome programme: three separate estimands, never merged -- two pooled within themselves, one reported from a single trial
question: In both phase 3 trials that supported sotagliflozin's approval, what is the effect of sotagliflozin compared with placebo on cardiovascular death and worsening heart failure -- counted as total events, counted as time to a first event, and on the three-component atherothrombotic endpoint -- with each of those questions answered separately?
_prose_rule: Every text field is PROSE unless it is on the validator's numeric list. Prose may not restate a number the object holds structurally.
_sourcing_rule: Every measured input carries the verbatim sentence it was read from and a resolvable link to the layer it was read from. Every cell records all five mandated source layers with a date, so a layer that held nothing is distinguishable from a layer nobody opened. Derived transforms are computed here and are not claimed to appear in any source.
_estimand_rule: THE LABEL ON THE QUANTITY IS NOT THE QUANTITY. Both trials' primary endpoints are RECURRENT-EVENT analyses counting first and subsequent events, and the journal, the registry and the regulator all report them as hazard ratios. This object files them by what the analysis did. It holds three estimands and pools across none of them; within them, the two that both trials report are pooled, and the third -- reported by a single trial -- is not pooled at all. No automated effect-measure check in this repository could enforce that -- which is why the separation is structural rather than a warning.
single_tier_because: The primary tier is NOT uniform in this object and that is worth stating, because it is unusual here: the two total-occurrence outcomes are sourced to the primary publications, while every cell of the time-to-first outcome is sourced to the FDA statistical review, because that review is the only staged layer on earth that prints those numbers. A cell's tier follows where its value actually came from.
completeness_statement: FULL BUILD over a NAMED PROGRAMME, with the boundary stated. Both phase 3 cardiovascular outcome trials of this drug are held and each contributes to every estimand it reports. There is exactly ONE source list, `screening.records`; `screening.excluded` is a view COMPUTED from it at build time, row for row, so it cannot say anything the records do not. What is NOT claimed is a systematic database search: the scope is the pivotal programme as the regulator's own review defines it, and the prior-synthesis search that WAS run is recorded with its terms, its results and its date in a staged file.

verification_basis.what_verifies_this_object: Two things, and neither is a badge this repository can emit about itself. The object is the single source of truth and the page is a pure projection of it, so a claim on the page that is not in the object cannot exist. And the object is read by two model families with independent file access, from different vendors, each asked to find a defect in the ACTUAL object rather than to approve it.
verification_basis.what_is_not_claimed: No internal check is described as independent verification. A script that reads this object and reports it consistent has confirmed consistency and nothing else. Note also what this object could NOT get: no published synthesis reports either trial's own primary as a separate row, so no independent re-analysis checks these values.
verification_basis.bar: Both families must find no defect in the object. A finding about the validator is not a finding about the object and does not block.

risk_of_bias.basis_in_sources: BOTH trials were terminated early because the sponsor withdrew funding, and THIS DOMAIN DOES NOT REST ON THAT. The usual stopped-early reasoning does not apply here: the danger with a trial stopped early FOR BENEFIT is an inflated effect at a data-dependent boundary, and the stop here was commercial, so there was no boundary to stop at. The early termination is named in this domain because any reader will look for it, and it is then explicitly SET ASIDE as a ground for it. An earlier version of this field said the object 'treats that as serious' and then argued in the next clause that it introduces no bias, which is a contradiction a gate leg was right to refuse. What carries the SERIOUS rating is internal validity alone: one trial changed its PRIMARY ENDPOINT during the trial, and both rest their primary analysis on investigator-reported rather than centrally adjudicated events. The lost power and lost follow-up that early termination also caused are NOT counted here -- they widen intervals rather than bias them, so they belong to imprecision, and an earlier version of this domain double-counted them. A gate leg was right that downgrading risk of bias for lost power is a misapplication of the domains. The endpoint change is the most serious of the three: it is exactly the condition that outcome-reporting-bias guidance is about, and it is recorded on the trial, on the cell and here.

inconsistency.derived_from: Q against its degrees of freedom and the between-study variance, both stored in this result's heterogeneity block. With so few studies the statistic has almost no power, so 'not serious' here means no heterogeneity was DETECTED and must not be read as evidence of agreement. Section 14.2.2 makes the trigger unexplained heterogeneity rather than a value of the statistic, and the one large clinical difference between these trials -- their populations -- is documented in the uniformity table rather than offered as a post-hoc explanation. Not downgraded, with that caveat stated rather than implied.

indirectness.basis_in_sources: Not downgraded, and the reasoning is worth stating because the opposite call is tempting. The frozen question is the drug across its PIVOTAL PROGRAMME, and the evidence is exactly that programme: the population, the intervention, the comparator and the outcomes are the ones the question names, measured in the trials themselves. The population SPREAD between the trials is real and large, but it is diversity WITHIN the question rather than a mismatch between the question and the evidence, and section 10.10.1 is where it belongs -- the uniformity table -- not here. An earlier version of this domain downgraded on the ground that a reader wanting a heart-failure answer would misread the pooled value. That is a risk of MISREADING, answered by labelling and by the scope block, and downgrading for it would be stricter than the Handbook while claiming the Handbook's support -- the same defect a gate leg caught on the companion review in this batch.

imprecision.triggers_computed: Condition one, the ordinary interval excluding the null: MET on every outcome here. Condition three, the optimal information size: NOT MET and not merely uncomputable -- both trials were terminated before they collected the information they were designed for, so whatever the target was, it was not reached. That alone is the ground for this downgrade and it is a fact about the trials, not a reading of a Handbook section. Two further observations point the same way and neither is offered as a rule: on the pooled outcomes an alternative interval method gives a range that includes the null, which section 10.10.4.5 says may be excessively wide at this number of studies and which is therefore reported rather than relied on; and on the single-trial outcome the upper bound sits just under the null, so the interval is consistent with a benefit too small to matter, which is condition two. An earlier version of this field made alternative-interval-crosses-null a downgrade RULE and credited it to 10.10.4.5, which does not give one.

Both trials also stopped early for funding, so neither reached the information it was designed to collect -- which is an argument for caution that the interval alone does not carry.

What remains true of both rows equally: this is a SENSITIVITY analysis of each trial's primary composite, performed and reported by the regulator, and in one of the trials the composite it re-analyses had itself been changed mid-trial. A pool of regulator sensitivity analyses is a legitimate quantity and it is not the same kind of evidence as a pool of prespecified primary endpoints. That does NOT show up as a different certainty rating here -- this outcome and the total-occurrence one carry the same rating from the same two downgrades -- and an earlier version of this row claimed it did.
ascertainment: BOTH stored cells use investigator-reported events, so the contributing rows do not differ on this axis and an earlier version of this row was wrong to say they did -- both review families caught it, and the companion outcome had always recorded the same situation as identical. What differs is not between the ROWS but between two analyses of each row: centrally adjudicated estimates exist for both trials, are stored beside each cell, and pool to a visibly different summary reported in the sensitivity block. Those are a SENSITIVITY analysis, not contributing rows. They are worth reading because the two bases move the two trials in OPPOSITE directions, which is the clearest signal in this object that ascertainment is not a rounding detail.

hfcv_first.heterogeneity_status: Computed from Q and its single degree of freedom. With TWO studies this statistic has almost no power to detect heterogeneity, so a low value is consistent both with agreement and with not being able to tell, and it is reported with that caveat rather than as reassurance. The difference these two trials genuinely have is in their POPULATIONS, and no statistic computed from two effect estimates can see it -- the uniformity table is the only place it is visible.

sensitivity.method: leave-one-out, a comparison of between-study variance estimators, and -- on the first-event estimand -- a parallel pool of the centrally adjudicated ascertainment
sensitivity.authority: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.14 for sensitivity analyses generally. Section 10.10.4.4 governs the estimator half: it records that methods other than DerSimonian and Laird estimate the between-study variance better and that restricted maximum likelihood is the current default. Section 10.10.4.5 is cited for the INTERVAL comparison and not for the estimator comparison; it concerns interpretation with few studies and the method it compares is the confidence interval.
sensitivity.decision_under_test: Whether the pooled estimate depends on either single trial, on the choice of between-study variance estimator and interval method, and -- where two ascertainment bases exist -- on which of them is used.
sensitivity.leave_one_out_finding: With two trials a leave-one-out fit IS the other trial, and this table says so rather than presenting single-trial rows as though they were pooled sensitivity results. Read it as what it is: the two trials' own estimates, side by side, with the interval each carries alone.

between_study_variance_method_comparison.why: Section 10.10.4.4 records restricted maximum likelihood as the current default and that estimators other than DerSimonian and Laird perform better; that is the whole of the authority for running this comparison. Nothing in the Handbook instructs a review to run it at a particular number of studies, and running it here is a choice made under 10.14 because with two trials the choice is plausibly influential.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.estimator_kept: Restricted maximum likelihood with the ordinary interval, because section 10.10.4.4 records it as the current default and as a better estimator than DerSimonian and Laird. The Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval is reported beside it with the floor on its scale factor applied, so it can widen and can never come out narrower than the ordinary one. It is NOT presented as the interval to prefer: section 10.10.4.5 says the opposite is possible, that with only two or three studies such intervals can be EXCESSIVELY WIDE and an ordinary interval may be preferable, and it asks for the comparison rather than for a winner. An earlier version of this field called it the interval to weigh most heavily, which attributed to that section a preference it does not express.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.verdict: Reported as computed rather than summarised in advance. Where the estimators agree it is because there is little between-study variance for them to disagree about, which at two studies is close to uninformative; where the conservative interval is much wider than the ordinary one, that width is the honest expression of how little two trials constrain a random-effects average, and section 10.10.4.5 says to expect it.

parallel_ascertainment_pool.finding: This is the same OUTCOME CONCEPT computed from the same document under the other ascertainment the regulator reports. The contributing rows of the pool above do NOT differ on ascertainment -- both are investigator-reported, and the uniformity table records that axis as identical. What is compared here is two ANALYSES of those same rows, which is why this sits in the sensitivity block and not in the table. It is the most informative sensitivity analysis in this object. The two bases move the two trials in OPPOSITE directions -- adjudication makes one trial's estimate less favourable and the other's more so -- which is why the pooled values sit close together while the per-trial values do not. A reader should take from this that the choice of ascertainment is not a rounding detail here, and that neither pooled number is the answer on its own.

cross_engine.engine: metafor 5.0.1 under R 4.6.0, generic inverse variance on the same log point and log standard error this object stores
cross_engine.agreement: Recomputed independently and checked against the stored values. This is two ENGINES agreeing on one arithmetic; it says nothing about whether the two TRIALS agree, and nothing at all about the population difference between them.
cross_engine.i2_definitions_differ: The two engines can report different values for the Higgins statistic and neither is wrong: this object's is computed from Q and its degrees of freedom, the other engine's relative to the restricted-maximum-likelihood between-study variance. They are different quantities sharing a name.

grade.certainty_derivation: start high; risk_of_bias serious (-1), imprecision serious (-1); total -2 -> low
grade.starting_point_because: both contributing studies are randomised controlled trials

risk_of_bias.basis_in_sources: BOTH trials were terminated early because the sponsor withdrew funding, and THIS DOMAIN DOES NOT REST ON THAT. The usual stopped-early reasoning does not apply here: the danger with a trial stopped early FOR BENEFIT is an inflated effect at a data-dependent boundary, and the stop here was commercial, so there was no boundary to stop at. The early termination is named in this domain because any reader will look for it, and it is then explicitly SET ASIDE as a ground for it. An earlier version of this field said the object 'treats that as serious' and then argued in the next clause that it introduces no bias, which is a contradiction a gate leg was right to refuse. What carries the SERIOUS rating is internal validity alone: one trial changed its PRIMARY ENDPOINT during the trial, and both rest their primary analysis on investigator-reported rather than centrally adjudicated events. The lost power and lost follow-up that early termination also caused are NOT counted here -- they widen intervals rather than bias them, so they belong to imprecision, and an earlier version of this domain double-counted them. A gate leg was right that downgrading risk of bias for lost power is a misapplication of the domains. The endpoint change is the most serious of the three: it is exactly the condition that outcome-reporting-bias guidance is about, and it is recorded on the trial, on the cell and here.

inconsistency.derived_from: Q against its degrees of freedom and the between-study variance, both stored in this result's heterogeneity block. With so few studies the statistic has almost no power, so 'not serious' here means no heterogeneity was DETECTED and must not be read as evidence of agreement. Section 14.2.2 makes the trigger unexplained heterogeneity rather than a value of the statistic, and the one large clinical difference between these trials -- their populations -- is documented in the uniformity table rather than offered as a post-hoc explanation. Not downgraded, with that caveat stated rather than implied.

indirectness.basis_in_sources: Not downgraded, and the reasoning is worth stating because the opposite call is tempting. The frozen question is the drug across its PIVOTAL PROGRAMME, and the evidence is exactly that programme: the population, the intervention, the comparator and the outcomes are the ones the question names, measured in the trials themselves. The population SPREAD between the trials is real and large, but it is diversity WITHIN the question rather than a mismatch between the question and the evidence, and section 10.10.1 is where it belongs -- the uniformity table -- not here. An earlier version of this domain downgraded on the ground that a reader wanting a heart-failure answer would misread the pooled value. That is a risk of MISREADING, answered by labelling and by the scope block, and downgrading for it would be stricter than the Handbook while claiming the Handbook's support -- the same defect a gate leg caught on the companion review in this batch.

imprecision.triggers_computed: Condition one, the ordinary interval excluding the null: MET on every outcome here. Condition three, the optimal information size: NOT MET and not merely uncomputable -- both trials were terminated before they collected the information they were designed for, so whatever the target was, it was not reached. That alone is the ground for this downgrade and it is a fact about the trials, not a reading of a Handbook section. Two further observations point the same way and neither is offered as a rule: on the pooled outcomes an alternative interval method gives a range that includes the null, which section 10.10.4.5 says may be excessively wide at this number of studies and which is therefore reported rather than relied on; and on the single-trial outcome the upper bound sits just under the null, so the interval is consistent with a benefit too small to matter, which is condition two. An earlier version of this field made alternative-interval-crosses-null a downgrade RULE and credited it to 10.10.4.5, which does not give one.
imprecision.derived_from: The pooled interval stored in this result, and the alternative-method interval reported beside it in the sensitivity block. Neither is turned into a threshold rule here: what carries the downgrade is the unmet information size recorded above, and the intervals are the arithmetic a reader can check it against. An earlier version of this field stated a rule that the triggers field two lines above explicitly disowned, and both review families found the contradiction.
imprecision.ois_note: The optimal information size is a condition section 14.2.2 makes part of adequate precision, and it is NOT computable from what this object holds: it needs an assumed control-arm risk and a target difference no field here carries. It is UNKNOWN rather than satisfied, and this sentence exists so its absence cannot read as a pass. Both trials also stopped early for funding, so neither reached the information it was designed to collect -- which is an argument for caution that the interval alone does not carry.

publication_bias.not_assessable_because: Far too few studies. Funnel-plot and regression methods for small-study effects are not interpretable at this size, so no assessment is made and none is implied. What can be said without a test is recorded instead: both trials are registered, both posted results, and both published their primary papers reporting the early termination. The mid-trial change of primary endpoint is reported in ONE of those papers, not in both -- an earlier version of this sentence credited it to both, which the object's own uniformity row already contradicted, and the regulator's review of both is public and staged here. Rated not assessable, which downgrades nothing on its own.

grade.what_this_certainty_is_about: The certainty of THIS estimand's pooled value and of nothing else. This object holds three estimands with three separate ratings, and they are not interchangeable: a reader who takes the rating from one and the number from another has produced a claim this object does not make. It is also a rating of a DRUG-WIDE average across two very different populations, not of the drug in heart failure.

handbook.decision: DO NOT POOL. One trial reports this endpoint in this form, so the result is that trial's own estimate, presented as such
handbook.conformance: There is no meta-analysis here and none is implied. The companion trial posts a total-occurrence composite of FOUR components -- these three plus hospitalization for heart failure -- so it differs from this cell in BOTH its event set and its unit of analysis, and the two differences are governed by DIFFERENT sections: the unit of analysis by 10.8 read against 10.9, and the EVENT SET by 3.2.4, under which a composite's components are part of how the review DEFINES its outcome -- so two composites differing in a component are two outcomes rather than two names for one. That is a limit on what may be POOLED, not a criterion for which trials are eligible: 3.2.4 cautions AGAINST letting eligibility depend on which outcomes a study reported, and this review's eligibility does not. An earlier version of this field read it the other way round and called the outcome a defining criterion of the review, which is the over-strict reading the object disowns elsewhere. An earlier version credited both to 10.9 alone, which is a time-to-event section and has nothing to say about which events a composite contains; an earlier version still called this the same three components, which was false of the registry record. Section 3.2.4 is also why this outcome is carried at all rather than dropped for being reported by only one trial: dropping it would make the review's content depend on what the studies chose to report.

per_trial.population: adults with type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 25 to 60, and cardiovascular risk; heart failure was NOT an entry requirement

sensitivity.authority: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.14. screening.search_note: The candidate set is the sotagliflozin PIVOTAL PROGRAMME as the regulator defines it -- the two phase 3 cardiovascular outcome trials that supported the US approval, both named in the staged integrated review -- together with the registry records for those trials and a check of the programme's other registered trials. That is what a drug-wide pivotal question needs, and it is described here as what it is rather than as a systematic database search.
screening.eligibility: ELIGIBILITY turns on population, intervention and comparator: a phase 3 randomised trial of sotagliflozin against placebo in the pivotal cardiovascular outcome programme. It does NOT turn on which analysis a trial reported -- section 3.2.4 cautions that eligibility resting on reported outcomes invites outcome reporting bias, and this object carries THREE estimands precisely so that a trial is not admitted or refused according to which one it happens to print. What the estimand governs is which POOL a value may enter, under section 10.9.
screening.known_limitation: No systematic database search was run and nothing here should be read as though one had been. The scope is a named two-trial programme, which is what the frozen question asks about, so the risk a search would address -- an eligible trial nobody named -- is small but not zero, and it is stated rather than assumed away. A separate and dated record of the prior-synthesis search that WAS run is staged beside this object.

records.identifier_note: The registry record whose official title reads SOTA-P-CARDIA Trial: A Randomized Trial of Sotagliflozin in HFpEF Patients Without Diabetes. An earlier version of this row carried a DIFFERENT accession, which had been written from recall rather than looked up and which belongs to an unrelated drug-interaction study in healthy volunteers. A gate leg resolved the identifier and caught it. A resolvable link to the wrong study is worse than no link, because it survives every check that only asks whether a link resolves.
records.reason: A sotagliflozin trial, and it is in this log rather than absent because a reader looking for the drug's trials will look for it. It is NOT part of the pivotal programme this object is scoped to: its registry record describes an investigator-sponsored later-phase mechanistic study in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction WITHOUT diabetes, with imaging and functional endpoints and an enrolment two orders of magnitude below either pivotal trial. An earlier version of this row called it part of the same programme, which a gate leg correctly read as false of the record. Its endpoints are cardiac and metabolic measures rather than the event composites this object holds, so it contributes to none of the three estimands. It is NOT excluded for reporting the wrong outcome in the sense section 3.2.4 warns against -- it reports no estimate of any of these three quantities at all, which is a different thing from reporting them and being ignored.
records.quantity_it_reports: cardiac and metabolic endpoints; no estimate of any composite this object holds

records.record_limitation: This row is written from the registry record and from the trial's place in the programme. Its results were not read for this object and no value from it is claimed, which is stated here rather than left for a reader to infer from the empty quantity field.

reconciliation.why_this_step_exists: Because on the first app in this batch it changed the answer, and on the second it recovered a correct benchmark that had been written off. Here it does a third thing: it establishes, with a dated record of the queries, that the synthesis this object would most want to check itself against does not appear to exist.
reconciliation.clean_because: Not clean, and the reason is an absence rather than a disagreement. No published synthesis reporting either trial's OWN primary endpoint as a separate row could be located, so the per-cell values in this object are checked against the regulator and the registry but against no independent synthesis. The one synthesis reconciled against includes one of these two trials and reports a harmonized endpoint this object does not hold, so it checks SCOPE and not VALUES. That is a real limit on how far this object has been checked and it is recorded rather than papered over.
reconciliation.access_limitation: The synthesis reconciled against is staged as its abstract; its full text is not open, which was established by querying the full-text archive for its identifier rather than inferred from a paywall notice. Its abstract NAMES all five of its trials, so the included-study list -- the thing this step needs -- is readable in full. Its per-trial rows are not, which is why no per-trial value is attributed to it anywhere in this object.

trial_list_diffs.review_scope: SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure across the ejection fraction spectrum, five randomised trials, fixed-effect, with endpoint definitions harmonized by the authors

SCORED is a diabetes and kidney-disease cardiovascular outcome trial, so it is correctly outside their scope and correctly inside this one. The two scopes disagree because they are different questions, not because either is wrong.

The synthesis's stated combined sample size is consistent with this object's denominators for the trial they share, given the four other trials it names.

corrections.item: the supplied first-event estimate for the worsening-heart-failure trial
corrections.review_reports: This object was handed a time-to-first estimate for that trial to carry, described as unverified.
corrections.this_object: It matches no analysis in the staged regulator review. The review reports two time-to-first estimates for that trial, on the two ascertainment bases, and the supplied figure is neither of them; its lower bound is the lower bound of one of them. Both real estimates are stored, the supplied one is stored nowhere.

corrections.item: which layer holds the time-to-first analysis at all
corrections.review_reports: The handoff expected the registry to be searched for it.
corrections.this_object: Neither registry posts it. Every posted outcome on both records is a total-occurrence or a change-from-baseline analysis. The quantity exists in exactly one staged document, the regulator's statistical review, which is recorded on each cell.

corrections.review_reports: The handoff recorded that the European application was withdrawn, which suggested an application for this indication that failed.
corrections.this_object: The European authorisation was GRANTED, in 2019, and for a different indication entirely -- an adjunct to insulin in type 1 diabetes. The staged medicine overview does not contain the phrase heart failure at all. It was later withdrawn at the holder's request for commercial reasons. So the European layer is not available for this endpoint because the EU authorisation was for type 1 diabetes and was withdrawn -- which is a different and more informative fact than a withdrawn application. What this object does NOT say, and what an earlier version of this sentence did say, is that there was never a European heart-failure assessment. The staged documents cannot establish that: an overview that omits a phrase is not a record of what was never filed. The corrected-claims block already made exactly that distinction, and this sentence had been contradicting it.

unresolved.item: no independent synthesis checks the values in this object
unresolved.detail: Four dated queries found no synthesis reporting either trial's own primary endpoint as a separate row, and the closest class-level network meta-analyses do not name either trial in their abstracts, so their included-study lists cannot be read from what is open. The consequence is stated plainly rather than minimised: the per-cell values here rest on the publication, the registry and the regulator, and on no independent re-analysis. A synthesis may exist behind a paywall or under indexing these queries did not reach.

Both total-occurrence cells differ between the FDA documents and the agreeing publication and registry -- on the lower bound for the smaller trial, on the point estimate for the larger. Within the FDA the two documents agree with each other on BOTH trials: an earlier version of this entry said they differed on the larger one, which was this object's own error and is corrected in the corrected-claims block. Nothing in the staged sources explains it. The review describes its analyses as based on investigator-reported events in all randomized patients, which is where an explanation would start, but the staged text does not say that it accounts for these differences and this object does not assert that it does.

claims_corrected.claim: that the worsening-heart-failure trial's time-to-first estimate is the value supplied to this build
claims_corrected.correction: The regulator's review reports two such estimates, one per ascertainment basis, and the supplied figure is neither. Its lower bound coincides with the lower bound of one of them, which is how a bound becomes an estimate in a chain of custody.

claims_corrected.claim: that the European application for this drug was withdrawn
claims_corrected.correction: An authorisation was granted and later withdrawn, and it was for insulin-dependent diabetes rather than heart failure. That is why the European layer holds nothing for this endpoint. What is NOT claimed, because the staged documents do not show it, is that a heart-failure indication was never applied for -- an overview that omits a phrase is not a record of what was never filed.

claims_corrected.claim: that this review can report one pooled effect for sotagliflozin
claims_corrected.correction: It holds three estimands and pools none of them together. The trials' own primary is a total-occurrence analysis reported as a hazard ratio; the time-to-first analysis of the same composite is a different set of numbers held only by the regulator; and the three-component first-occurrence endpoint is reported by one trial. A single headline would have to merge at least two of those.

claims_corrected.claim: that the two FDA documents disagree with each other about the larger trial's total-occurrence primary endpoint
claims_corrected.correction: They agree to every digit. The review's PRIMARY endpoint analysis and the label's efficacy table print the same interval, and the differing lower bound this object had quoted from the review belongs to a SENSITIVITY analysis on the same endpoint -- the one censoring non-cardiovascular deaths as non-informative. A value was matched across documents without the ANALYSIS it belongs to, which is the defect this object's own cascade exists to prevent, committed by the object itself and built into a headline before a gate leg caught it. The surviving divergence is real and unchanged: the publication and the registry print a different point estimate from the one both FDA documents print. The companion trial was re-checked the same way and needed no correction -- there the review's primary line and the label's table do print the interval this object records.

SCOPE:three-estimands-never-merged.decision: The total-occurrence composite, the time-to-first analysis of that same composite, and the three-component first-occurrence endpoint are three separate outcomes, each with its own result block and its own certainty rating, and no value crosses between them. TWO of them are pooled; the third is reported by a single trial and is not pooled at all, which its own result block says on its face. An earlier version of this sentence claimed three separate POOLS, which implied a synthesis for that third outcome that the sources do not support and that the structured result correctly refuses.
SCOPE:three-estimands-never-merged.conformance: Section 10.9 fixes what may be combined: log hazard ratios for the same quantity by generic inverse variance. A proportional-rates analysis over first and subsequent events and a Cox analysis of the time to a first event are not the same quantity, and every layer here calls both of them a hazard ratio -- which is precisely why the separation has to be structural rather than a note. Section 3.2.4 is why all three are carried instead of only the one the trials designated primary.

SCOPE:the-label-on-the-quantity-is-not-t.decision: A value is filed by what the analysis DID, never by what the source called it. Both trials' primary endpoints are recurrent-event analyses reported as hazard ratios by the journal, the registry and the regulator alike, and they are filed as total-occurrence estimands.
SCOPE:the-label-on-the-quantity-is-not-t.conformance: This is the single most load-bearing decision in the object and the one no automated check in this repository could make for it: an effect-measure detector sees two hazard ratios and is satisfied. The companion review in this batch EXCLUDED one of these very trials for this reason. This object includes it and separates the estimands instead, which is a different answer to the same fact and is defensible only because the separation is structural.

SCOPE:publication-two-component-first-ev.decision: The larger trial's publication reports a first-occurrence composite of cardiovascular death OR hospitalization for heart failure -- TWO components, without urgent heart failure visits. This object does not use it for the time-to-first estimand and stores no value from it. The time-to-first estimand here is the time-to-first analysis of that trial's OWN primary composite, which has three components, and the regulator's review is the only staged layer that prints it. Treating the publication's two-component figure as the same cell would put a different event set under the same name -- the conflation this object exists to refuse -- and it would also re-source a load-bearing row to a layer that does not print it.
SCOPE:publication-two-component-first-ev.conformance: Section 3.2.4 governs which outcomes a review defines and how they are grouped. A composite is defined by its event set, so two composites differing in a component are two outcomes and not two labels for one. Section 10.9 governs the time-to-event analysis the two share, which is exactly why the shared analysis type is not sufficient to make them one cell. This block exists because an earlier version of the time-to-first cascade cell said this composite was 'recorded in the screening and scope blocks rather than silently used here' when it was recorded in NEITHER -- a cross-reference that pointed at nothing. A gate leg found it; this block is the record the sentence claimed.

SCOPE:drug-wide-pivotal-not-heart-failur.decision: The question is the drug across its pivotal programme, so both trials are in and the pooled value spans a heart-failure population and a diabetes-and-kidney-disease population. The heart-failure-only result is a labelled SUBGROUP -- one trial's own row -- and never the headline.
SCOPE:drug-wide-pivotal-not-heart-failur.conformance: Section 3.2.1 makes the population a defining criterion, and this object defines it as the pivotal programme rather than as a disease. That is a legitimate question and it is also the one most open to being misread, so the population difference is the largest row in every uniformity table here. It is deliberately NOT a reason to downgrade indirectness: the frozen question IS the drug-wide programme, so the spread is diversity WITHIN the question rather than a mismatch with it, and it is carried under section 10.10.1 in the uniformity table instead. An earlier version of this sentence said the indirectness domain was downgraded for it, which contradicted the GRADE blocks themselves; a gate leg found the contradiction by reading both.

SCOPE:no-number-needed-to-treat.decision: No absolute risk reduction and no number needed to treat is computed or displayed anywhere in this object, on any outcome.
SCOPE:no-number-needed-to-treat.conformance: On the total-occurrence outcome the arithmetic is not merely unhelpful, it has no meaning in the usual sense: the denominator of a number needed to treat is a difference in the PROPORTION of people with an event, and this endpoint counts events rather than people. On the other two outcomes it would need an assumed control risk over a stated horizon that no field here carries. The renderer computes none, which was checked rather than assumed.
